clue.text: Pass over friend in the neighbourhood

indicators.note: over signals turning the mountain-pass word back to front

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend living nearby is passed over for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns COL (a mountain pass) into LOC, and ALLY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done locally happens close by, in the surrounding area.

clue.text: Spend freely to get flogging abolished

parts.note: a lash is a stroke of the whip, a flogging
something abolished is out, done away with

explanation.surface: A campaigner splashes money to have corporal punishment banned.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is an idiom for spending lavishly on something.

clue.text: Irate testimonial directing one to look at another page

definitions.text: directing one to look at another page

parts.note: cross means angry, irate
a reference is a written testimonial from an employer

explanation.surface: An angry letter of recommendation sends the reader elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A note in a book pointing the reader to a different page or section for related material.

clue.text: Evangelistic physician shows the French around the United Kingdom

indicators.note: around means the French article is wrapped about the country's abbreviation

parts.note: le is French for the
UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A gospel-preaching doctor gives French visitors a tour of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Luke, author of the third Gospel, is described by Paul as 'the beloved physician'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gospel writer traditionally held to have been a doctor by profession.

clue.text: Moving jerkily after an American gin cocktail

parts.note: Yank is slang for an American

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drinker staggers after an American's gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING, placed after YANK.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull with a sudden sharp tug, so this is pulling in jerks.

clue.text: See! The firm is crazy

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone points out that the company is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is Spanish-derived slang for mad.

clue.text: Despicable intimate details

definitions.meaning: the inside facts or full information on a matter

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means base and mean; as a noun it is slang for the inside information.

clue.text: She cleans out the fish

definitions.meaning: a charwoman or cleaner who cleans houses
a freshwater fish related to the trout

explanation.surface: A woman guts the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a domestic cleaner, and the Arctic char is a salmon-family fish.

clue.text: Pa dared to run riot and joined the procession

indicators.note: running riot is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A father bravely ran wild and then fell in with a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to run riot' rearranges PA DARED into the answer; the held text 'Dad dared' is a misreading of the printed 'Pa dared'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have paraded is to have marched in a procession.

clue.text: Youngsters in the swim from Kingsley

definitions.text: Youngsters in the swim from Kingsley

parts.words: Youngsters in the swim from Kingsley
parts.note: the children who live underwater in Charles Kingsley's Victorian novel, the title of the book itself

explanation.walkthrough: Charles Kingsley was a Victorian writer; his famous children's book is titled after these water-dwelling infants.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley's 1863 novel is about a chimney sweep turned into a child living in a river.

clue.text: Electric storm?

parts.note: read playfully, a thunderstorm gives a jolt of electricity and is also very bad weather

explanation.definitionFit: A storm with lightning both shocks with electricity and is dreadful weather.

clue.text: River's oxygen has a purpose

definitions.note: River's stands for river is, the 's being a link

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a use is a purpose

explanation.surface: Oxygen in the river serves a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, notably in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English rivers bear this name, including the Great Ouse.

clue.text: He has unreasonable faith in a large part ofthe Bible

parts.note: big means large
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A believer holds blind faith in a large portion of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot clings intolerantly to an opinion or creed regardless of reason.

clue.text: Due to make an appeal over marriage

indicators.note: over places the exclamation before the marriage word

parts.note: O is an exclamation of entreaty, as in 'O Lord'
wed means to marry, standing here for marriage

explanation.surface: Someone pleads about a forthcoming wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is due is owing, still to be paid.

clue.text: At length do the same

definitions.meaning: do. is the abbreviation, so written out at length it becomes the full word
used in lists to mean as before, likewise

explanation.walkthrough: 'At length' means written in full, so 'do' here is the abbreviation expanded.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation do. stands for this word, which means as above or likewise.

clue.text: A fellow spy

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man is a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is a spy working for an intelligence service.

clue.text: It's entrusted to the best man in Wagnerian operas

definitions.text: It's entrusted to the best man
definitions.meaning: at a wedding the best man looks after the band to be placed on the bride's finger
Wagner's four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen is known by this short name

explanation.definitionFit: The wedding band held by the groomsman, and the common English name of Wagner's operatic cycle.

clue.text: Denied the necessity to carry a gun

indicators.note: to carry means the necessity word holds the gun word inside it

parts.note: a need is a necessity
gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Someone was refused the need to bear arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts GAT, gangster slang for a pistol, inside NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have negated something is to have nullified or denied it.

clue.text: A superior criminal assistant

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: A top-class accomplice in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abets helps another commit a crime, an accomplice.

clue.text: In danger of causing a triple crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A three-car pile-up puts people at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being imperilled or at risk means facing danger.

clue.text: A weird, wee infant, but sweet

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or weird
baba is a nursery word for a baby

explanation.surface: A strange little baby turns out to be sweet natured.
explanation.walkthrough: A rum baba is a small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup; 'sweet' is a British word for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of yeast sponge soaked in rum syrup.

clue.text: To extract this from the ground needs manlier resolution

definitions.text: To extract this from the ground

indicators.note: resolution in the sense of breaking up and reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mining takes more masculine determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like determination but signals the anagram of MANLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ores and other inorganic substances are dug out of the earth by mining.

clue.text: Servicemen found in the airmen's mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn up in the air force canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the dining hall but rearranges AIRMENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the naval infantry corps are servicemen.

clue.text: Pound payment made in advance to sailors lightens the gloom

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the thing that brightens darkness

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling
an ante is a stake paid before play
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Paying sailors up front cheers everyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp in a case brightens darkness.

clue.text: Disheartened pioneer becomes a mole

indicators.note: the heart of the word pioneer is cut out of its middle

explanation.surface: A discouraged explorer turns into a burrowing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes ONE from the centre of PIONEER. A mole here is a stone breakwater, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a jetty or breakwater built out into the sea.

clue.text: Fashionable Sunday trading centre

parts.note: a mart is a market, a trading centre

explanation.surface: A trendy market is open on Sundays.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means stylish or chic.

clue.text: The thread of the story

definitions.meaning: spun fibre used for knitting or weaving

explanation.surface: The plot line of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both spun fibre for knitting and a rambling tale.

clue.text: Fatuous piece of humour gains a following

indicators.note: following places the a after the joke word

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A silly joke wins fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means foolish or senile.

clue.text: Some nasty eye-infection

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A rather unpleasant infection of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'naSTY Eye', and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: What show-jumpers may do to beat the clock

definitions.text: What show-jumpers may do to beat the clock

parts.words: What show-jumpers may do to beat the clock
parts.note: in a timed jump-off riders hurry round the course, and the phrase is also the idiom for working urgently to a deadline

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurrying to finish before a deadline, literally a timed round in show jumping.

clue.text: Laugh at the barrier

definitions.meaning: the sound of laughter written out
a sunken fence or ditch bounding a park without blocking the view

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is written laughter, and also a sunk fence in landscaped grounds.

clue.text: Letit stand, boy, in top gear

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A father tells his son to leave it alone while driving fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' looks like a car's highest gear but means headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat is something worn on top.
